source_review.notes: Reviewed eight sources covering Little's law, queueing theory, performance modeling, staged event-driven architecture, enterprise messaging patterns, distributed data, tail latency, and site reliability. DOI metadata confirmed the Little, Harchol-Balter, SEDA, and Tail at Scale publication identities and dates; the current official Google SRE book index was retrieved. No mutable broker-product behavior is asserted.

evidence: Reviewed cumulative arrivals and service, in-system work, arrival/service rates, utilization, Little's-law population/time variables, deadlines, age, business identity, attempts, partitions, net drain, and amplification notation.
Confirmed Little's-law variables share one population boundary and rate-duration products yield item counts.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Queueing delay, sojourn, admission, delivery, effect, and terminal business outcome remain distinct.

evidence: Recomputed 200 jobs/s times 5 seconds as average 1,000 jobs in system.
Recomputed overload (1,100-800) times 120 seconds as 36,000 jobs and later drain at 300 jobs/s as 120 seconds.
Recomputed exercise values: 300 times 8 = 2,400 jobs; (450-300) times 600 = 90,000; drain at 120 jobs/s = 750 seconds or 12.5 minutes.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Freshness counterexamples show why storage and eventual drain do not establish useful completion.

evidence: Verified Little's-law use L=lambda W under stable consistent population boundaries.
Verified fluid backlog growth as (lambda-mu)T only during constant positive excess.
Verified drain time B/(mu-lambda_r) only when continuing arrivals remain strictly below service.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The fluid model is explicitly not a stochastic tail-latency, skew, payload-cost, or failure-correlation model.

evidence: Reviewed stable average with deadline failure, arrival equal to and greater than service, sustained overload, one hot tenant, and a stopped partition.
Reviewed crash before and after external effect, lost acknowledgement, short and long visibility, duplicate, reorder, poison, expiry, and dead-letter redrive.
Reviewed oversized hostile payload, compromised producer, downstream connection saturation, reconnect herd, and physical-command staleness.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cases span capacity, correctness, freshness, ordering, fairness, security, recovery, and physical safety.

evidence: Traced durable business identity, admission scope, deadline revalidation, idempotent effect, lease fencing, retry bounds, poison isolation, tenant fairness, and priority authorization through examples and answers.
Confirmed empty broker state and delivery acknowledgements never substitute for reconciled business outcomes.
invariant_checking.notes: Coalescing is restricted to domain-valid set-state semantics and excluded from additive or audit history.

evidence: Reviewed Little's-law calculation and confirmed consistent average-population and sojourn boundaries.
Reviewed the overload/drain derivation and confirmed finite drain requires positive spare service after ongoing arrivals.
Reviewed the payment redelivery counterexample and confirmed broker delivery semantics cannot make an external provider effect atomic.
proof_review.notes: No queue, retry, FIFO, or autoscaling mechanism receives guarantees beyond its explicit boundary.

evidence: Audited uses of stable, durable, accepted, delivered, processed, complete, ordered, idempotent, exactly-once, current, expired, recovered, and safe.
Verified accounting law, approximation, protocol mechanism, domain policy, observed evidence, and business guarantee remain separated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Successful enqueue and queue emptiness are explicitly bounded evidence.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter prescribes load, skew, retry, broker-failover, and restoration experiments but reports no executed queue deployment or wildfire-response exercise.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed acceptance, temporal decoupling, Little's law, bursts, multidimensional bounds, backpressure, shedding, freshness, identity, visibility, retries, dead letters, ordering, partitioning, fairness, scaling, durability, multi-stage flow, security, outcomes, and testing for coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed stable Little measurement, burst/drain, email acceptance, visibility mismatch, poison FIFO, database-limited autoscaling, tenant domination, coalescing, payment ambiguity, and empty-queue reconciliation. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate-depth capacity and lifecycle reasoning, sixteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar international wildfire-response transfer problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source checks and calculations do not constitute a live overload, poison-message, external-payment, broker-failover, wildfire-response, or physical-command experiment.
